howItWorks.title: How {name} works
howItWorks.intro: {name} runs your questions against a synthetic population — thousands of simulated respondents calibrated to real demographic data — so you can see how people would likely react before you spend a single dollar on a real panel.

population.title: A calibrated population, not a guess
population.body: Each simulated respondent ("agent") carries real demographic and behavioral attributes — age, income, region, attitudes — built to match the composition of your target population. You can audit that composition at any time, comparing the simulated shares against the real shares of your source axes.

direction.title: The answer is never "A", "B" or "C"
direction.body: When we put a question to the synthetic panel, we don't ask for — or trust — a single "correct" answer. Just like a real survey, we aggregate hundreds or thousands of independent responses and report the statistical distribution: which option gathered more support, what direction an effect moved between groups, and how reliable that difference is. The platform never states an answer as "the truth" — it shows the direction and strength of the signal, with the caveats that belong to it.

flow.title: From draft to result
flow.body: Define your target population, your stimulus and your response instrument, run the experiment, and get back real statistics plus an AI-written narrative that never invents a number — it only explains what has already been computed.

exposure_mode.direct_assignment_desc: Every agent sees the stimulus and answers directly — like a traditional survey. Use this to measure the whole population's reaction at once, with no simulation of how the information spreads.
exposure_mode.channel_diffusion_desc: The stimulus spreads gradually through the population, entering via a channel (social media, TV, internal rumor, etc.) and passing person to person. Only agents who became "exposed" form an opinion. Use this to compare diffusion channels or measure adoption over time — the trade-off is the extra setup of a channel, reach and diffusion rate.

synthesizer.independent_quota_v1_desc: Samples each attribute independently from marginal quotas.
synthesizer.ipf_v1_desc: Iterative proportional fitting to match joint distributions.

grounding_compiler.generic_llm_v1_desc: Uses the LLM without additional grounding.
grounding_compiler.persona_demographic_v1_desc: Grounds each agent in its demographic attributes.
grounding_compiler.persona_profile_v1_desc: Grounds each agent in all of its available evidence, uniformly and without provenance.
grounding_compiler.population_grounded_v1_desc: Grounds responses in the population distribution.
grounding_compiler.evidence_grounded_v1_desc: Grounds responses in evidence and benchmarks.

item_type.conjoint_profile_choice_desc: Presents stimulus profiles for the agent to choose from.

analysis_module.attribute_distribution_desc: Distribution of values per attribute across the population.
analysis_module.representativeness_chi2_desc: Chi-square goodness-of-fit of the observed population against reference targets.
analysis_module.segment_breakdown_desc: Breaks results down by population segments.
analysis_module.response_fidelity_correlation_desc: Pearson correlation between the human and synthetic value per respondent.
analysis_module.decision_fidelity_winner_desc: Checks whether the synthetic population picks the same winner as humans.
analysis_module.bootstrap_robustness_desc: Bootstrap confidence interval of the human-vs-synthetic mean absolute error.
analysis_module.structural_drivers_eta2_desc: How much of the answer variance each attribute explains (weighted eta²).
analysis_module.amce_conjoint_desc: Average marginal effect of each attribute value on the outcome.
analysis_module.cross_profile_desc: Crosses the two highest-eta² attributes and shows the rate per combined cell.
analysis_module.channel_segment_comparison_desc: For each segment, which channel produced the best market response (adoption).
analysis_module.treatment_effect_categorical_desc: Compares this arm's effect over control (gap between two categories) in human vs. synthetic data. Requires pointing at the control arm's run.
analysis_module.subgroup_heterogeneity_fidelity_desc: Compares the human vs. synthetic outcome distribution within each value of a respondent attribute (e.g. vaccination status).
analysis_module.conjoint_stimulus_amce_desc: Average marginal effect of each STIMULUS/PROFILE attribute level (e.g. efficacy, country of origin) on the chance of being chosen — distinct from AMCE by respondent attribute.
analysis_module.conjoint_stimulus_amce_by_subgroup_desc: The same stimulus AMCE, computed separately for each value of a respondent attribute (e.g. party) — tests interactions like partisan reversal on an endorsement attribute.
